::: {.callout-note}
Written with the SDTM (F3 day 5) and completed with the clinical study report, after the
database lock (tag `dblock-301`). The study is still blinded (ADR 0032): the package is the
blinded one. The structure follows the PHUSE cSDRG template. The data are simulated and the
sponsor is fictional.
:::

## 1. Introduction

The package holds the SDTM datasets of FJF-2026-301, a 26-week, randomised, double-blind,
placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase III study of FJF-2026 20 mg added to metformin in
adults with type 2 diabetes. Datasets are SAS transport v5 files, described by `define.xml`
(Define-XML 2.1). Standards: SDTM 2.0, SDTMIG 3.4, CDISC SDTM terminology 2024-03-29.

The datasets are built from the raw (EDC-like) layer by the project's pipeline, from the
specification `docs/specs/sdtm-301.yml` and the cleaning rules `docs/specs/cleaning-rules.yml`.

## 2. Protocol description

Two arms, 1:1, stratified by screening HbA1c (≤ 8.5%, > 8.5%): placebo + metformin and
FJF-2026 20 mg + metformin. Screening (2 weeks), treatment (26 weeks), follow-up (2 weeks). The
trial design is in TA, TE, TV, TI and TS; each subject's path is in SE.

## 3. Subject data description

### Domains

| Dataset | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DM | Demographics | Screen failures included (ARMNRS = SCREEN FAILURE). |
| DS | Disposition | Protocol milestones and disposition events. |
| IE | Criteria not met | Screen failures only, from the criterion recorded on the CRF. |
| SV | Subject visits | Unscheduled visits numbered after the previous planned visit (+ 0.1). |
| SE | Subject elements | Screening, treatment, follow-up; EPOCH of every other domain comes from SE. |
| EX, DA | Exposure, product accountability | One EX record per bottle; tablet counts in DA. |
| CM | Concomitant medications | Background therapy and rescue medication (CMCAT). |
| AE, SUPPAE | Adverse events | SUPPAE.AEENRAW holds end dates set aside by rule CR08. |
| CE, SUPPCE | Hypoglycaemic events | ADA level in CESCAT; glucose and assistance in SUPPCE. |
| LB, VS | Laboratory, vital signs | Standard units by fixed factors; height from the screening demography page. |

### Coding dictionaries

MedDRA and WHODrug need a licence. Adverse events and medications are coded with the
project's own reduced dictionary (`docs/specs/coding-dictionary.yml`): MedDRA-like lowest level
term, preferred term and system organ class, without codes, and ATC level 4 classes for
medications. AELLTCD, AEPTCD, AEHLT, AEHLGT and their codes are therefore absent.

### Data that are not collected

- **COUNTRY** is empty: the CRF does not collect the country of the site.
- **Seriousness criteria** (AESHOSP, AESDTH, ...) are not collected; only AESER is.
- **Demography of screen failures** is not collected, so their SEX, RACE and BRTHDTC are empty.

### Cleaning rules applied in SDTM

The raw layer is never changed. Duplicates keep the first entry (CR01), partial dates stay
partial (CR02), weights in pounds and heights in metres are converted in the standard result
variables (CR04, CR05), laboratory units are converted with fixed factors (CR06), qualified
results stay as text (CR07), and an adverse event end date before its start is moved to SUPPAE
(CR08). Every record a rule touches is listed in the data-issues listing.

### Blinding

The database is locked (tag `dblock-301`, `docs/lock/dblock-301.yml`) but the study is not
unblinded: locking and unblinding are two decisions, and the pipeline uses the real
assignment only after the reviewer authorises the unblinding (ADR 0032). Until then the arm of
each subject in DM, SE and EX (ARMCD, ARM, ACTARMCD, ACTARM, EXTRT, EXDOSE) comes from a dummy
assignment: the real arms shuffled within stratum with a public seed (ADR 0027). Every other
variable is final. After an authorised unblinding the package is rebuilt by the same programs,
and only the treatment variables change.

## 4. Data conformance summary

Pinnacle 21 Community 2304.3 (SDTM-IG 3.4, FDA) reports no reject and no define.xml issue.
CDISC CORE v1.0.0 (SDTMIG 3.4 published rules) was run before the lock. Each remaining issue
of either tool is explained in `studies/301/conformance.md`. A second, independent programming
(`qc/301/sdtm_qc.R`) agrees with production in every domain it covers.
